messages:
akshay: Hey all — day 1 here. Quick sheepish ask: who owns what across infra / repos / oncall? I'm blocked on VPN and a couple of repo perms. Any tiny map or who-to-ping list?

lisa: welcome Akshay! :tada: Short map off the top:
- repos: @sam (infra) for org repos, @maria for product docs repos
- infra/GCE/VPC: infra team -> #eng-infra and sam
- models & runtime: eng-runtime (reach out to gabe)
- billing/quotas: finance slack or billing@redwood.com
- oncall/escalation: eng-oncall rotation via PagerDuty (see oncall-bot)

sam: hey — for VPN + Okta MFA, file the self-serve request here: https://internal/redwood/onboarding-vpn (choose "Day 0 network"). If you need repo access, ping me with the repo name and I'll add you. Typical command we ask to verify: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood.com/v1/whoami
```
(Ignore the $TOKEN part if you haven't got one yet, just paste your GitHub handle)

maria: added a one-pager for day 1 access in the new-hires channel — https://docs.redwood.com/onboarding/day1-access. Also tag me if something is timing-critical and I’ll nudges infra. Please join the #new-hires-intros thread too so we can route hardware & laptop pickups.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty rotation for eng-oncall: primary this week -> @jeff; backup -> @nina. For SEV1 page eng-oncall immediately: https://pagerduty.com/redwood/eng-oncall. If you need to escalate to security, page sec-oncall.

gabe: addition on escalation:
- SEV1: page eng-oncall (PD) AND DM the primary owner listed in our runbook for the service.
- SEV2: open a ticket in #incidents and assign to owner, put "SEV2" in the subject.
- Non-urgent / access: email infra-support@redwood.com or ping #eng-infra.
Runbook index (short): https://internal/redwood/runbooks/service-ownership (owners + backups).

akshay: this is super helpful, thanks everyone. I'll ping sam with repo names and hit the VPN link. One tiny follow-up — if I page eng-oncall accidentally, what's the preferred apology/close flow?

lisa: no stress — message the channel and mark the incident as "false alarm" in PagerDuty, drop a one-line note with what went wrong, e.g., "mistaken alert — forgot VPN token." People appreciate the quick note.

akshay: got it, thanks. Will join the intros thread and upload my laptop pickup form. :slightly_smiling_face:
